items.title: 2026-022: Critical vulnerabilities in Nginx
items.summary: F5 disclosed five NGINX vulnerabilities allowing unauthenticated remote code execution as the worker process; a PoC exists for CVE-2026-123007 but no in-the-wild exploitation yet. Patch internet-facing instances first.

items.title: 2026-020: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway
items.summary: Citrix patched 28 memory flaws in NetScaler ADC and Gateway; CVE-2026-120868 affects all deployments including default configurations, with unpredictable behaviour and DoS impact. No exploitation reported.

items.title: Peace in Ukraine won’t end Russian sabotage in Europe, Poland warns
items.summary: Poland's intelligence minister warns that Russian hybrid and sabotage operations against Europe will likely continue regardless of the outcome of Ukraine peace talks.

items.title: Microsoft Azure flaw exploited to steal customers' API credentials
items.summary: Microsoft warns that a flaw in Azure API Management Classic tiers was exploited to steal stored API credentials; Norwegian authorities link it to attacks on energy companies.

items.title: Daily summary - 23.11.2026
items.summary: CERT.at reports active internet exploitation of flaws in Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver and VMware vCenter, plus a Rackspace Spot breach exposing customer Kubernetes secrets.

items.title: 354 dark web vendors and buyers arrested in Europol-coordinated global crackdown
items.summary: Operation TorNado, coordinated by Europol across 14 countries, led to 354 arrests of dark web vendors and buyers between May 2025 and October 2026, targeting cybercrime, drugs and firearms.

items.title: 2026-021: High Severity Vulnerability in Java SE and OpenJDK
items.summary: Oracle and OpenJDK fixed CVE-2026-114938, a high-severity flaw that can lead to unauthenticated RCE under certain conditions. CERT-EU advises prioritising internet-facing Java applications.

items.title: Ransomware gangs keep multiplying, even as fewer victims pay
items.summary: Check Point Research counted 2,830 ransomware victims on leak sites in Q3 2026, a record quarterly total, with a growing number of active groups even as fewer victims pay ransoms.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco Unveil AI-Assisted Linux Security Tool to Block Exploits Before Patching
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime letting AI agents write dynamic eBPF controls that block exploit behaviour without downtime, buying time before patching.

items.title: Hackers Exploit N-able MailAssure Flaw While AI Agents Exploit MONAI Label Zero-Day

items.title: Linux patches can take weeks, and OpenAI and Cisco built Shirudo to help in the meantime
items.summary: Deeper look at Shirudo, the OpenAI/Cisco open-source tool that applies temporary, restart-free mitigations to running Linux systems while patches are tested and deployed.

items.title: Hackers breach Austrian Foreign Ministry website, access diplomats' contact details
items.summary: Austria's Foreign Ministry confirmed attackers breached one of its websites and obtained names and official contact details of staff in Vienna and at diplomatic missions abroad.

items.title: Industrial Serial Gateways Broadcast That They're Insecure
items.summary: Research finds industrial serial gateways openly advertise whether authentication is enabled, and many internet-exposed OT access devices are unprotected.

items.title: Inception - possibly a ShinyHunters reboot - claims seven victims in a week
items.summary: A group calling itself Inception, possibly a ShinyHunters rebrand, claimed seven victims in a week; voice phishing is reported as a key access technique.

items.title: CrowdStrike Makes AI Security Push With Blockbuster Zscaler Deal

items.summary: OpenRouter removed three AI inference providers after finding they breached stated data-handling policies and exposed prompts and secrets — a reminder of AI supply chain risk.

items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-133968 (MONAI Label path traversal) and CVE-2026-134624 (N-able Mail Assure SSRF) to the KEV catalog based on active exploitation; BOD 26-04 deadlines apply to US federal agencies.

items.summary: Estonia's foreign minister explains the decision to close the border with Russia, arguing sustained pressure is needed to force a ceasefire.

items.title: 5 ways Europe could revamp its security architecture to please Putin and Trump
items.summary: Politico outlines five scenarios for reshaping European security architecture under pressure from Washington and Moscow during Ukraine peace talks.

items.summary: SANS ISC reports sustained scanning activity over 90 days from subnet 109.160.32.0/24, assigned to Romanian VPS provider BANATSYNC SRL (AS198364).

items.summary: UN Secretary-General Guterres urged the world to agree on AI oversight mechanisms within a year.

items.summary: NATO's chief pledged defences against space-based threats after German media reported Russia plans to launch a satellite carrying a nuclear warhead.

items.summary: The Register covers Shirudo, the Cisco/OpenAI eBPF-based project that generates compensating controls quickly to reduce exposure windows before patching.

items.summary: Meta launched its AI agent Muse in the UK, with regulators expected to watch the rollout closely.

items.summary: Guidance on shadow accounts and delegated password management, highlighting risks when departments create and share credentials without IT oversight.

items.title: Orgs that leak data ‘prioritize corporate interests over customers’ says Have I Been Pwned’s Troy Hunt
items.summary: Troy Hunt of Have I Been Pwned criticises breached organisations for prioritising corporate interests over customers, describing a pattern of denial, delay and legal threats.

items.summary: Stalwart 1.2.0, an open-source mail server, adds MAPI over HTTP, EWS, ActiveSync and Autodiscover support, positioning it as an on-prem Exchange alternative under AGPL.

items.summary: Analysis of Taiwan's elections and Beijing's commentary on them, with implications for regional stability.

items.title: Trump to meet NATO chief ​Mark Rutte on Wednesday, White House says
items.summary: The White House says President Trump will meet NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte on Wednesday.

items.summary: Singapore is investigating Nvidia-linked firm Megaspeed following its US blacklisting, touching on AI chip export control enforcement.

items.summary: Qatar's prime minister says he is working to revive US-Iran talks and de-escalate tensions after meeting Secretary Rubio.

items.summary: Chinese lab Z.ai released GLM-5.4, its first model using a looped transformer architecture that iterates weight-shared layers for greater depth without more parameters.

items.summary: Virginia and Oregon filed lawsuits against SpaceX alleging weak safeguards in Grok allowed generation of CSAM and nudified imagery.

items.summary: Oregon and Virginia attorneys general sued several Musk companies over alleged weak safeguards against sexualized deepfake imagery generated by Grok.

items.title: Project MONAI MONAI Label Path Traversal Vulnerability
items.summary: Project MONAI MONAI Label contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to write arbitrary files outside the intended datastore directory, potentially resulting in remote code execution.

items.title: N-able MailAssure (SpamExperts) Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability
items.summary: N-able MailAssure (SpamExperts) contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the LDAP synchronization connection check that allows an authenticated API user to connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, determine which are reachable, and send crafted data to internal services.

items.title: Hardcoded JWT signing key in AutoGPT
items.summary: AutoGPT versions 0.6.26 through 0.7.4 include a publicly known default key used for HS256 JWT validation. An attacker can create tokens for arbitrary users or administrative roles when a deployment continues to use that default key.
items.mitigation: Upgrade AutoGPT to version 0.8.0. Replace any default JWT secret with a unique deployment-specific value and invalidate tokens issued under the old key.

items.title: Authentication bypass through token type confusion in xo-server
items.summary: xo-server REST authentication can accept parsed cookie data where a token identifier should be a string. A remote unauthenticated attacker may be authenticated as the owner of an available unexpired token and obtain reusable token identifiers; exploitation depends on such a token being present.
items.mitigation: Update the XO deployment containing xo-server to fixed release 6.9.2 or 6.10.1, as appropriate for the deployment's release line. Until updated, restrict access to the REST service to trusted networks.

items.title: Authentication bypass in Kerberos Agent
items.summary: Kerberos Agent versions before 3.14.4 can accept administrator tokens signed with a known fallback JWT key. An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the affected API may gain administrative access, expose camera-related secrets, change configuration, or stop the camera service.
items.mitigation: Upgrade Kerberos Agent to version 3.14.4 or later. Restrict network access to its API and configuration interfaces until the upgrade is complete.
